 With

 In Fast/15124/2019
 Eknath Nama Gume
 Versus
 The State Of Maharashtra And Anr
 ...
 Mr. Suraj V. Gundre, Advocate for Applicants.
 Mr. V. M. Jaware, Agp for Respondent No.1
 ...
 Coram : S. G. Chapalgaonkar, J.
 Dated : 12th February, 2024.
 Per Court:-
 1.

The applicants/original claimants in Land Acquisition
 References seek to condone the delay of 2113 days caused in filing
 the First Appeals against the awards passed by the Reference
 Court.
2.  Mr. Gundre, learned Advocate appearing for the  applicants submits that the lands of the applicants have been  acquired in the year 2005.
They were granted inadequate  compensation by the Land Acquisition Officer.
Therefore, the  applicants had preferred Land Acquisition References under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act.
Although the applicants  have laid sufficient evidence to indicate that they are entitled for  the compensation as claimed
, the learned Reference Court  granted limited enhancement.
He would further submit that  although award was passed in the year 2013, the respondents  have deposited the compensation amount in the month of July  (2) 54-ca-5601-2020.odt 2018.

After receiving the said amount, the applicants could manage for expenses for filing the First Appeals and accordingly Eknath Nama Gume vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49914978/

sentences.text: the delay is caused, which is unintentional.
Therefore, they seek to condone the delay and register the First Appeals.
3. The learned A.G.P. strongly opposes the prayer.
4. Although the notice is served upon respondent no.2- Acquiring Body, none appears for them.
5. The contentions in these applications have gone uncontested.
Therefore, the case is made out for condoning the delay.

However, on condition that the applicants shall not claim interest for the period of delay and file such an undertaking with the Registrar (Judicial) of this Court within a period of eight weeks from today.

Hence, following order:
 ORDER a.
Civil Applications are allowed.

b. Delay of 2113 days caused in filing the First Appeals is hereby condoned subject to condition that the applicants file an undertaking to the Registrar (Judicial) of this Court within a period of eight weeks from today that they shall not claim interest for the delayed period, in case this Court awards enhanced compensation in Appeals.
c. First Appeals be registered.
d. Civil Applications are disposed of.
(S. G. CHAPALGAONKAR)
JUDGE Devendra/February-2024
